Teratogenic effects have been reported in animals. Effects on the liver. Use of ethionamide or protionamide with rifampicin for the treatment of multibacillary leprosy has been associated with a high incidence of hepatotoxicity. A hepatitis incidence of 4.5 to 5% has been reported for patients on ethiona- mide or protionamide, rifampicin, and either dapsone or clofaz- imine.1,2 In these studies, diagnosis of hepatitis was based on clinical assessment. When laboratory monitoring was used, an incidence of 13% was reported with a regimen of ethionamide or protionamide with rifampicin and dapsone.3 A regimen of pro- tionamide, dapsone, rifampicin, and clofazimine has been asso- ciated with a 22% incidence based on laboratory monitoring.4 Use of ethionamide with pyrazinamide has also resulted in a high incidence of abnormal liver function tests.5 In the above studies rifampicin was given daily during part or all of the regimens. The incidence of hepatotoxicity when ethiona- mide or protionamide is used with once-monthly rifampicin may be lower; hepatotoxicity was not reported in patients receiving monthly rifampicin and daily protionamide, isoniazid, and dap- sone.6 1.
